DataSourceSetupGuide({'steps': [{'label': 'Create a Stripe restricted API key', 'detail': 'Generate a read-only restricted key in the Stripe Dashboard.', 'kind': 'app_config', 'instructions': "- Open the Stripe Dashboard: https://dashboard.stripe.com/apikeys
- Click **Create restricted key** (produces a key starting with `rk_live_...` or `rk_test_...`).
- Give it a name like `holmes-mcp-read`.
- Set these resource permissions to **Read**: Charges, Customers, PaymentIntents, Disputes (and any other resources you want Holmes to read, e.g. Refunds, Balance, Payouts).
- Leave everything else as **None** so the key is read-only.
- Click **Create key**, copy the token, and store it in your password manager - Stripe won't show it again.
- Keep the token handy for the next step; you'll put it in a Kubernetes secret and never in the Helm values.", 'command': '', 'yaml': ''}, {'label': 'Create the Kubernetes secret', 'detail': "Stores the Stripe restricted key in the runner's namespace so Holmes can read it.", 'kind': 'secret', 'instructions': '', 'command': "kubectl create secret generic stripe-mcp-token -n robusta --from-literal=token='<paste-your-stripe-restricted-key>'", 'yaml': ''}, {'label': 'Add the Stripe MCP server to your Helm values', 'detail': 'Merge this snippet into your existing generated_values.yaml (do not create a new file).', 'kind': 'helm', 'instructions': '', 'command': '', 'yaml': 'holmes:
  additionalEnvVars:
    - name: STRIPE_MCP_TOKEN
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:
          name: stripe-mcp-token
          key: token
  mcp_servers:
    stripe:
      description: "Stripe MCP server - read Stripe payments, charges, customers, and disputes."
      icon_url: "https://stripe.com/favicon.ico"
      docs_url: "https://docs.stripe.com/mcp"
      config:
        url: "https://mcp.stripe.com"
        mode: streamable-http
        headers:
          Authorization: "Bearer <env.STRIPE_MCP_TOKEN>"
      llm_instructions: |
        ## When to use
        Use Stripe when the user asks about **payments**, **charges**, **customers**, or **disputes** in Stripe - for example investigating a failed charge, checking a customer's payment history, looking up a specific `pi_...` / `ch_...` / `cus_...` / `dp_...` ID, or triaging a dispute.

        ## Preferred tools (read-only)
        - `stripe_api_read` for direct API `GET` calls - e.g. `GET /v1/charges/{id}`, `GET /v1/customers/{id}`, `GET /v1/payment_intents/{id}`, `GET /v1/disputes/{id}`, `GET /v1/charges?customer=...`.
        - `stripe_api_search` / `stripe_api_details` when you're not sure which endpoint or parameters to use.
        - `search_stripe_resources` / `fetch_stripe_resources` to look up an object by ID or free-text query across payments, charges, customers, disputes.
        - `get_stripe_account_info` to confirm which Stripe account is being queried.
        - `search_stripe_documentation` when the user asks a conceptual Stripe question.

        ## Rules
        - **Do not** call `stripe_api_write`, `create_refund`, or any mutating tool - the configured key is read-only and the user only asked for read access.
        - Always pass the concrete Stripe object ID when the user provides one (starts with `pi_`, `ch_`, `cus_`, `dp_`, `re_`, etc.).
        - Include relevant fields (amount, currency, status, failure reason, dispute reason) in your answer so the user doesn't need to open the Dashboard.'}, {'label': 'Apply the change', 'detail': 'Runs helm upgrade so Holmes picks up the new data source.', 'kind': 'deploy', 'instructions': '', 'command': 'helm upgrade robusta robusta/robusta --values=generated_values.yaml --set clusterName=alon-elish-cluster', 'yaml': ''}, {'label': 'Verify the connection', 'detail': 'Confirm Holmes loaded the Stripe MCP server and can call it.', 'kind': 'verify', 'instructions': '- Wait for the `helm upgrade` to complete and the Holmes pod in namespace `robusta` to restart (`kubectl get pods -n robusta -w`).
- Open Robusta's **Data Sources** list and confirm **Stripe** appears and is healthy.
- Ask Holmes a read query, e.g. *"Look up Stripe charge ch_xxx and tell me its status and any dispute"* or *"Show the last 5 payment_intents for customer cus_xxx"*.
- If it fails auth, double-check the secret with `kubectl get secret stripe-mcp-token -n robusta` and that the token has the expected Read permissions in the Stripe Dashboard.', 'command': '', 'yaml': ''}]})

DataSourceSetupGuide({'steps': [{'label': 'Create a Stripe restricted API key', 'detail': 'Grant read-only scopes for the resources Holmes needs.', 'kind': 'app_config', 'instructions': "- Sign in to the Stripe Dashboard and open **Developers → API keys → Restricted keys**.
- Click **Create restricted key** and give it a name like `holmes-readonly`.
- Set these permissions to **Read** (leave everything else at **None**):
  - Core → Charges
  - Core → Customers
  - Core → PaymentIntents
  - Core → Payments (if listed separately)
  - Core → Disputes
- Create the key and copy the `rk_live_...` (or `rk_test_...`) value. You'll pass it to the secret in the next step.
- Reference: https://docs.stripe.com/keys/restricted-api-keys
- Reference: https://docs.stripe.com/mcp", 'command': '', 'yaml': ''}, {'label': 'Create the Kubernetes secret', 'detail': 'Stores your Stripe restricted key so Holmes can read it at runtime.', 'kind': 'secret', 'instructions': '', 'command': "kubectl create secret generic stripe-mcp-credentials -n robusta --from-literal=token='rk_live_replace_me'", 'yaml': ''}, {'label': 'Add the Helm values', 'detail': 'Merge this snippet into your existing generated_values.yaml.', 'kind': 'helm', 'instructions': '', 'command': '', 'yaml': 'holmes:
  additionalEnvVars:
    - name: STRIPE_API_KEY
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:
          name: stripe-mcp-credentials
          key: token

  mcp_servers:
    stripe:
      description: "Stripe payments platform (hosted MCP server at mcp.stripe.com)"
      icon_url: "https://cdn.simpleicons.org/stripe/635BFF"
      docs_url: "https://docs.stripe.com/mcp"
      config:
        url: "https://mcp.stripe.com"
        mode: streamable-http
        headers:
          Authorization: "Bearer <env.STRIPE_API_KEY>"
      llm_instructions: |
        ## When to use
        Use Stripe when investigating anything involving a **payment**, **charge**, **customer**, or **dispute** in Stripe - e.g. a failed payment, a chargeback, a refund question, or looking up a customer's payment history.

        ## Preferred tools (read-only)
        - `stripe_api_read` - fetch specific Stripe resources by ID via GET endpoints. Prefer this for `charges`, `payment_intents`, `customers`, and `disputes`.
        - `fetch_stripe_resources` - retrieve a Stripe object when you have its ID.
        - `search_stripe_resources` - find charges, customers, payment intents, or disputes by email, metadata, amount, status, or time range when the ID is unknown.
        - `stripe_api_search` / `stripe_api_details` - discover the right API method and its parameters before calling `stripe_api_read`.
        - `search_stripe_documentation` - answer "how does Stripe X work" questions from official docs.

        ## Rules
        - **Do not** call `stripe_api_write` or `create_refund` (or any other mutating tool). This integration is scoped to reading data only.
        - Prefer narrow, ID-based reads over broad searches when you already have an ID.
        - Always report the resource `id`, `status`, `amount`, `currency`, and `created` timestamp when summarizing a payment, charge, or dispute.'}, {'label': 'Apply the Helm upgrade', 'detail': 'Rolls out the new data source on cluster alon-elish-cluster.', 'kind': 'deploy', 'instructions': '', 'command': 'helm upgrade robusta robusta/robusta --values=generated_values.yaml --set clusterName=alon-elish-cluster', 'yaml': ''}, {'label': 'Verify the connection', 'detail': 'Confirm Stripe shows up as a data source and Holmes can query it.', 'kind': 'verify', 'instructions': '- Wait for the Helm upgrade to finish and the Holmes pod in the `robusta` namespace to restart and become Ready.
- Open the Robusta UI and check that **Stripe** appears in the Data Sources list as enabled.
- Ask Holmes something that exercises the integration, for example:
  - `Look up Stripe charge ch_xxx and show its status and amount`
  - `Find recent Stripe disputes in the last 7 days`
  - `Show the last 5 payment intents for customer cus_xxx`
- If the toolset shows as disabled, check the Holmes pod logs for a Stripe auth error and confirm the `stripe-mcp-credentials` secret has the correct `rk_...` key.', 'command': '', 'yaml': ''}]})

DataSourceSetupGuide({'steps': [{'label': 'Create a Stripe restricted API key', 'detail': 'Create a read-only restricted key in the Stripe Dashboard for Holmes to use.', 'kind': 'app_config', 'instructions': '- Go to the Stripe Dashboard API keys page and click **Create restricted key**.
- https://dashboard.stripe.com/apikeys/create
- Name it something like `holmes-mcp-readonly`.
- Grant **Read** permission on: **Payments (PaymentIntents)**, **Charges**, **Customers**, and **Disputes**. Leave everything else as **None**.
- Click **Create key** and copy the value (starts with `rk_live_...` or `rk_test_...`).
- Use test mode first if you want to try it safely.
- Docs: https://docs.stripe.com/keys/restricted-api-keys', 'command': '', 'yaml': ''}, {'label': 'Create the Kubernetes secret', 'detail': 'Store the Stripe restricted key in a secret the Robusta runner can read.', 'kind': 'secret', 'instructions': '', 'command': "kubectl create secret generic stripe-mcp-token -n robusta --from-literal=token='<your-rk_-key>'", 'yaml': ''}, {'label': 'Add the Helm values', 'detail': 'Merge into your existing generated_values.yaml under holmes:', 'kind': 'helm', 'instructions': '', 'command': '', 'yaml': 'holmes:
  additionalEnvVars:
    - name: STRIPE_MCP_TOKEN
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:
          name: stripe-mcp-token
          key: token
  mcp_servers:
    stripe:
      description: "Stripe MCP server - read payments, charges, customers, and disputes from Stripe."
      icon_url: "https://stripe.com/favicon.ico"
      docs_url: "https://docs.stripe.com/mcp"
      config:
        url: "https://mcp.stripe.com"
        mode: streamable-http
        headers:
          Authorization: "Bearer <env.STRIPE_MCP_TOKEN>"
      llm_instructions: |
        ## When to use
        Use this server whenever the user asks about **Stripe** payments, charges, customers, or disputes (e.g. "why did charge `ch_...` fail", "look up customer `cus_...`", "list recent disputes", "show payment intent `pi_...`").

        ## Preferred tools (read-only)
        - `stripe_api_read` - primary tool for reading Stripe resources. Use it against these endpoints:
          - `GET /v1/payment_intents` and `GET /v1/payment_intents/{id}` for payments
          - `GET /v1/charges` and `GET /v1/charges/{id}` for charges
          - `GET /v1/customers` and `GET /v1/customers/{id}` for customers
          - `GET /v1/disputes` and `GET /v1/disputes/{id}` for disputes
        - `stripe_api_search` / `stripe_api_details` when you need to discover the right endpoint or its parameters.
        - `search_stripe_resources` / `fetch_stripe_resources` for quick lookups by object ID.
        - `search_stripe_documentation` when clarifying Stripe concepts or error codes.

        ## Constraints
        - **Do NOT** call `stripe_api_write`, `create_refund`, or any other mutating tool - the configured restricted key is read-only and this data source is for investigation only.
        - Always pass real Stripe IDs from the user (`pi_...`, `ch_...`, `cus_...`, `dp_...`); do not invent IDs.
        - Prefer listing with filters (e.g. `customer=cus_...`, `created[gte]=...`) over unbounded scans.
'}, {'label': 'Apply the change', 'detail': 'Run the Helm upgrade so Holmes picks up the new data source.', 'kind': 'deploy', 'instructions': '', 'command': 'helm upgrade robusta robusta/robusta --values=generated_values.yaml --set clusterName=alon-elish-cluster', 'yaml': ''}, {'label': 'Verify the connection', 'detail': 'Confirm Holmes can talk to Stripe.', 'kind': 'verify', 'instructions': '- Wait for the Helm upgrade to finish and the Holmes pod in the `robusta` namespace to restart and become `Ready`.
- Open the Data Sources page in Robusta and confirm **Stripe** appears in the list.
- Ask Holmes something like: *"List my 5 most recent Stripe charges"* or *"Show details for customer cus_XXX"* and confirm you get real Stripe data back.
- If it fails, check the Holmes pod logs and confirm the `stripe-mcp-token` secret exists in the `robusta` namespace and the restricted key has the right read permissions.', 'command': '', 'yaml': ''}]})
